# Evervault — Style Reference

> Black-indigo vault glass, ciphertext etched on the walls, one violet lamp. Roobert Medium headlines over Inter, a #010314 canvas, 1px #1d1f2e hairlines with crosshair terminals, and a single violet accent rationed to toggles, badges and one gradient.

**Theme:** dark

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Evervault speaks a vault-at-night product language. The canvas is #010314, an ink-indigo just off black. On top of it sit #0b0d1c panels for the ledger mockup and #ffffff0f frosted tiles, which with 26 uses are the most frequent fill. Surfaces are layered by translucency rather than by lightness steps. The chromatic budget is one hue: violet, split between #8e64ff for toggles, links and glow and #6633ee for "New" badges. A single exception is #3ddc97, reserved for approved-transaction status. Typography carries hierarchy through size alone. Roobert Medium 500 at 56px and 40px, tracked at -0.02em and -0.01em, sits over Inter 400 body at 16px and 14.4px. The 29.6px, 40px and 56px steps climb by roughly 1.4, which is steeper than a Perfect Fourth. Monospace ciphertext strings are the only ornament. Shape is split into four values: 100px pills for actions, 4px tiles, 16px content cards and 24px showcase frames. Elevation comes from 1px #1d1f2e hairlines and inset rings, and one violet glow is reserved for the primary pill. The page reads as an encrypted terminal staged as a brochure rather than a fintech marketing site.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Onyx Canvas | `#010314` | `--color-onyx-canvas` | Page background, section fields and primary-pill label text (9 fills, 4 text uses). The indigo undertone keeps the black from going dead and lets the violet read as native light. |
| Carbon Panel | `#0b0d1c` | `--color-carbon-panel` | Transaction ledger body, decryption-key popover and the dark nav capsule. It is the single opaque lift above canvas, so solid surfaces are deliberately scarce. |
| Frosted Tile | `#ffffff0f` | `--color-frosted-tile` | Product tiles, icon frames and inactive chip fills (26 uses, the most common background). It is white at 6% alpha, so depth is a veil rather than a gray step. |
| Paper Ink | `#ffffffe6` | `--color-paper-ink` | H1, H2 and card titles, plus body emphasis (71 uses). It is white at 90% alpha, which takes the glare off pure white on a near-black field. |
| Fog Caption | `#ffffff99` | `--color-fog-caption` | Paragraph copy, product subtitles and ciphertext strings (44 uses). This 60% alpha is the reading tone, and most of the page's words live here. |
| Ash Label | `#ffffff80` | `--color-ash-label` | Ledger column labels, vertical margin captions and footer meta (31 uses). It is the tertiary tier and should not carry sentences longer than one line. |
| Pewter Meta | `#8e8fa0` | `--color-pewter-meta` | Announcement-bar labels and "Learn more" links (8 uses). It is the only opaque gray in the system and belongs to chrome, not to content. |
| Iron Border | `#1d1f2e` | `--color-iron-border` | Ledger outlines, announcement-bar rule and section crosshair lines, always at 1px. It is the hairline that replaces shadow almost everywhere. |
| Chalk Fill | `#ffffff` | `--color-chalk-fill` | Primary pill fill and toggle knobs. It is the system's actual primary action color, an inverted chip rather than a branded fill. Do not dilute it with violet. |
| Lilac Haze | `#bea7ff1a` | `--color-lilac-haze` | Secondary "Sign up" pill and ghost action fills. It is a 10% lavender wash that tints the frosted language just enough to read as clickable. |
| Iris Badge | `#6633ee` | `--color-iris-badge` | "New" and "Free" micro-badges and announcement chips (13 uses). It is the deeper violet, used only as a solid fill under white text. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |
| Amethyst Signal | `#8e64ff` | `--color-amethyst-signal` | Toggle-on state, links, gradient origin and primary-pill glow. It is the brand's single saturated hue and functions as light, not paint. Do not flood sections with it beyond the one gradient panel. |
| Mint Pulse | `#3ddc97` | `--color-mint-pulse` | "Approved" status text and acceptance-rate figures (12 uses). It is a status-only green, so it never fills buttons or backgrounds. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Roobert — the display voice for every headline and category eyebrow · `--font-roobert`

- **Substitute:** Hanken Grotesk at 450, Schibsted Grotesk at 450, Manrope at 500. Roobert Medium draws lighter than its nominal 500 and renders closer to a 450, so heavier grotesks at true 500 will look bolder than the original.
- **Weights:** 500, 600
- **Sizes:** 14.4px, 29.6px, 40px, 56px
- **Line height:** 1.1, 1.2
- **Letter spacing:** -1.12px at 56px, -0.4px at 40px, 0px at 29.6px, 0.576px at 14.4px (uppercase)
- **OpenType features:** `"blwf", "cv03", "cv04", "cv09", "cv11"`
- **Role:** Medium 500 at display sizes is the signature. Headlines are large but quiet, which is anti-convention for fintech, where 700 headlines are the norm. The steps from 29.6px to 40px to 56px rise by roughly 1.35 and then 1.4, steeper than a Perfect Fourth (1.333). That leaves the middle of the scale empty and makes every headline an event. Tracking tightens proportionally with size (-0.02em at 56px), while the 600 uppercase eyebrow opens up to +0.04em to act as a label. The cv-alternates soften the geometry so the face reads technical without turning robotic.

### Inter — the UI and body workhorse for paragraphs, nav, buttons and ledger figures · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter itself at 400 and 500 (open source), Geist at 400 and 500, IBM Plex Sans at 400 and 500. Inter renders true to its nominal weight, so match numbers directly.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 10px, 11px, 12.8px, 13px, 14px, 14.4px, 16px, 24px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.2, 1.4, 1.45, 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** -0.32px at 16px, -0.288px at 14.4px (500), -0.24px at 24px (700), -0.13px at 13px (500), 0px at 12.8px, 0.4px at 10px (700), 0.44px at 11px, 0.65px at 13px (uppercase)
- **Role:** Inter at 400 does the reading and Inter 700 does the counting, as in the $55,710.30 totals and the 10px uppercase ledger labels. Body text is tracked at -0.02em at 16px, which runs tighter than Inter's default and pulls paragraphs toward Roobert's compressed rhythm. Micro sizes open up to +0.04em so 10px labels survive on a near-black field. The 8.5px Inter in the hero ledger is mockup-internal and is not part of the scale.

### ui-monospace — the ciphertext face for encrypted card tokens · `--font-ui-monospace`

- **Substitute:** JetBrains Mono at 400, Geist Mono at 400, IBM Plex Mono at 400. All three match the thin system-mono stroke, and Plex at 400 should not be swapped up to 500.
- **Weights:** 400
- **Sizes:** 12px
- **Line height:** 1.2
- **Letter spacing:** -0.12px at 12px
- **Role:** Mono appears only where data is encrypted, in strings such as EV:K3D6:NEQ6GZZE in ledger rows and the scrolling character field between sections. It is the brand's proof device rather than a code-snippet face. The slight -0.01em tracking makes token strings read as dense, opaque blocks. IBM Plex Mono, Geist Mono, Geologica and Montserrat appear inside the card illustration only and are mockup-internal.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Inter | 700 | 10px | 1.2 | 0.4px | `--text-small` |
| caption | ui-monospace | 400 | 12px | 1.2 | -0.12px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 400 | 12.8px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 400 | 14.4px | 1.45 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Inter | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | -0.32px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Inter | 700 | 24px | 1.2 | -0.24px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Roobert | 500 | 29.6px | 1.2 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Roobert | 500 | 40px | 1.2 | -0.4px | `--text-heading` |
| display | Roobert | 500 | 56px | 1.2 | -1.12px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Roobert at weight 500, 56px for display and 40px for section heads — volume comes from size and -0.02em tracking, not from boldness.
- Keep the canvas at #010314 and lift surfaces with #ffffff0f alpha veils — tonal translucency preserves the indigo undertone that an opaque gray would flatten.
- Make the primary action a #ffffff pill at a 100px radius with #010314 text — the brightest object on a dark page outranks any colored button.
- Ration violet: #8e64ff for toggles, links, glow and one gradient panel, and #6633ee only for 10px badges — a single hue keeps its meaning as "Evervault" because it is scarce.
- Draw structure with 1px #1d1f2e hairlines and "+" crosshair terminals — the engineering-drawing frame does the work that drop shadows do elsewhere.
- Render every encrypted value in ui-monospace at 12px in #ffffff99 — ciphertext is the brand's proof, so it must look like real data.
- Run interior spacing on 10px and 12px and section spacing on 80px — the 2px half-step keeps dense ledgers tight while the page breathes.

### Don't

- Don't set headlines at Roobert 600 or Inter 700 at 56px — the restraint of weight 500 at display sizes is the thesis, and bold headlines turn the vault into a sales banner.
- Don't fill the primary button with #8e64ff — violet is light in this system, and making it the CTA paint spends the entire chromatic budget on one control.
- Don't introduce a second brand hue such as cyan or orange for feature highlights — the budget of one violet plus status-only #3ddc97 is non-negotiable.
- Don't use pure #ffffff for paragraph text — body copy sits at #ffffff99 and headlines at #ffffffe6, and full white flattens a hierarchy that depends on alpha.
- Don't round product tiles to 16px or 24px — 4px corners are what separate the parts catalogue from the 16px showcase cards.
- Don't add soft gray drop shadows to cards on #010314 — they vanish on near-black and muddy the 1px #1d1f2e hairline system.
- Don't decorate with stock illustration or 3D blobs — ornament here is never anything but ciphertext, line-art isometric icons and the single violet gradient.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #010314 (Onyx Canvas)
- elevated surface: #0b0d1c (Carbon Panel)
- glass tile: #ffffff0f (Frosted Tile)
- primary text: #ffffffe6 (Paper Ink)
- body text: #ffffff99 (Fog Caption)
- hairline: #1d1f2e (Iron Border)
- accent: #8e64ff (Amethyst Signal)
- primary action: #ffffff (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts take #8e64ff as a single solid series with every other series in #ffffff80 or #ffffff0f fills, and positive outcomes such as approval rates are expressed as #3ddc97 text or 2px lines rather than filled bars, so the violet gradient panel stays the loudest color on any page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: an inline-flex pill with background #ffffff, text color #010314, no border, border-radius 100px and padding 12px 24px. Set the label in Inter at 14px weight 500 with line-height 1 and add a trailing right-arrow icon with a 6px gap. Apply box-shadow `rgba(0,0,0,0.34) 0px 0.36px 1.52px -1.5px, rgba(0,0,0,0.29) 0px 1.37px 5.77px -3px, rgba(0,0,0,0.04) 0px 6px 25.2px -4.5px, rgba(141,99,255,0.2) 0px 2px 15px 0px`. Place a secondary sibling 10px to the right with background #bea7ff1a, text #ffffff, the same radius and padding, and box-shadow `rgba(190,167,255,0.12) 0px 0px 0px 1px inset`.

2. Build a Navigation Bar on a #010314 background with a 1200px max-width and three zones. On the left, place a white wordmark. In the center, place a capsule with background #0b0d1c, border-radius 20px, height 32px and padding 0 12px, using box-shadow `rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0px 0px 0px 2px, rgba(255,255,255,0.1) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(255,255,255,0.5) 0px 0.5px 0px 0px inset`, containing seven links in Inter at 13px weight 500 with -0.13px letter-spacing in #ffffffe6, spaced 20px apart. On the right, place a "Log in" text link in the same type and a #ffffff primary pill at radius 100px.

3. Build a Transaction Ledger Card with background #0b0d1c, a 1px solid #1d1f2e border, border-radius 16px and width 580px. Give it five rows with padding 10px 12px, divided by 1px #1d1f2e rules. Each row holds a 4px-radius card-brand chip, a token string in ui-monospace at 12px weight 400 with -0.12px tracking in #ffffff99, a "✓ APPROVED" label in Inter at 10px weight 700 uppercase with 0.4px tracking in #3ddc97, and a right-aligned amount in Inter at 12.8px weight 700 in #ffffffe6. Add a footer at 24px padding with a "TOTAL VOLUME" label in Inter at 10px weight 700 in #ffffff80, a figure in Inter at 24px weight 700 with -0.24px tracking in #ffffffe6, and a right-aligned rate in the same style colored #3ddc97.

4. Build a Feature Column: a heading in Roobert at 14.4px weight 600, uppercase with 0.576px letter-spacing in #ffffffe6, followed 18px below by a paragraph in Inter at 14.4px weight 400 with line-height 1.45 in #ffffff99. Add a 1px #1d1f2e rule with "+" glyphs at both ends, 24px below the paragraph. Below the rule, stack Product Tiles at a 12px gap, each with background #ffffff0f, a 1px #1d1f2e border, border-radius 4px and padding 4px. Each tile holds a 4px-radius line-art icon frame, a title in Inter at 14.4px weight 500 with -0.288px tracking in #ffffffe6, and a subtitle in Inter at 12.8px in #ffffff99. Optionally pin a "New" badge with background #6633ee, text #ffffff in Inter at 10px, radius 4px and padding 2px 4px to the top-right corner.

### Layout

- **Page max-width:** 1200px (360–1200px)
- **Section gap:** 80px (60–120px)
- **Card padding:** 24px (18–32px)
- **Element gap:** 10px (4–24px)

## Components

### Pill Button — Chalk (Primary)

**Role:** The single filled call to action

An inverted chip. The fill is #ffffff with #010314 text, there is no border, and the radius is 100px. Padding is 12px 24px, giving roughly 38px of height, and the label is set in Inter at 14px weight 500 with a trailing arrow glyph. The shadow is the md stack, which ends in a 15px violet halo at rgba(141, 99, 255, 0.2). The primary action is the brightest object on a dark page rather than the most colorful one. Use it once per viewport, for "Book a demo", "Get started" and "Talk to an Expert".

### Pill Button — Lilac Haze (Secondary)

**Role:** Ghost action beside the primary

A tinted glass pill. The fill is #bea7ff1a with #ffffff text, there is no border, the radius is 100px and padding is 12px 24px. The label is Inter at 14px weight 500, and a subtle-2 inset ring at rgba(190, 167, 255, 0.12) defines the edge. This is the measured "Sign up" spec. It sits directly next to the Chalk pill with a 10px gap and reads as a quieter sibling rather than as a bordered outline button, which is the anti-convention choice for a secondary action.

### Navigation Bar

**Role:** Floating centered link capsule

A three-part header on canvas. The wordmark sits left. In the center is a link capsule with a #0b0d1c fill and a 20px radius, wrapped in the subtle ring shadow, 32px tall (estimated), and holding Inter links at 13px weight 500 with -0.13px tracking in #ffffffe6. On the right are a "Log in" text link and the Chalk primary pill. The capsule floats in the middle instead of spanning the width, so navigation reads as an instrument panel rather than a toolbar.

### Announcement Bar

**Role:** Top-of-page product launch strip

A one-line ribbon. It is set on #010314 with a 1px #1d1f2e bottom rule and 10px vertical padding. It holds an Iris Badge "New" chip in #6633ee, a bold label in Inter at 12.8px weight 700 in #8e8fa0, descriptive copy at 12.8px weight 400 in #6b6580 (announcement-only and not a system token), and a "Learn more" link at weight 500. The muted grays keep launch news below the hero in volume.

### Transaction Ledger Card (Main Content Card)

**Role:** Hero product proof surface

The signature showcase. The fill is #0b0d1c with a 1px #1d1f2e border and a 16px radius. Rows sit on 10px vertical padding and are divided by 1px #1d1f2e rules. Each row holds a ui-monospace 12px #ffffff99 token string, a processor chip, a 10px weight-700 #3ddc97 "APPROVED" status and an Inter 700 amount in #ffffffe6. The footer total is Inter at 24px weight 700. The card is a working interface, never an illustration.

### Product Tile

**Role:** Capability entry in category columns

A compact list cell. The fill is #ffffff0f with a 1px #1d1f2e border, a 4px radius and 4px padding around a 4px-radius icon frame drawn in line-art isometric strokes. The title is Inter at 14.4px weight 500 with -0.288px tracking in #ffffffe6, and the subtitle is Inter at 12.8px in #ffffff99. Tiles stack with a 12px gap. The near-square 4px corners make the grid read as a parts catalogue rather than as marketing cards.

### Category Eyebrow with Crosshair Rule

**Role:** Column header and divider

A typographic label. The text is Roobert at 14.4px weight 600, uppercase with 0.576px tracking, in #ffffffe6. It sits 18px above a paragraph in #ffffff99. Below it runs a 1px #1d1f2e rule terminated by small "+" crosshair glyphs at both ends. This crosshair motif repeats at section corners, and it frames the page like an engineering drawing rather than a layout grid.

### Status Badge — Always On

**Role:** Locked-feature indicator in config panels

A tinted micro-chip. The fill is Amethyst Signal at 15% alpha (#8e64ff26, a derived tint and not a system token), the text is #8e64ff with a check glyph, and the label is Inter at 10px weight 700, uppercase with 0.4px tracking. The radius is 4px and padding is 2px 6px. The badge marks immovable features like Encryption and Relay, and it is the only place violet appears as text.

### New Badge

**Role:** Launch flag on tiles

The solid violet exception. The fill is #6633ee, the text is #ffffff in Inter at 10px weight 400, the radius is 4px and padding is 2px 4px. It is pinned to the top-right corner of a Product Tile at a -6px offset. This is the one place the deeper violet is allowed as an opaque fill, because a few square pixels of saturation work as punctuation rather than decoration.

### Toggle Switch

**Role:** Feature enablement control

A tiny pill switch. The on-state track is #8e64ff and the off-state track is #ffffff1f (a mockup-internal alpha, not a system token). The radius is 20px, padding is 2px and the switch is 14px tall. The #ffffff knob carries the sm shadow at rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) 0px 2px 8px. Violet appears here precisely because the toggle is the user's decision.

### Text Input

**Role:** Inline form field

A borderless field. The background is transparent and the text is #ffffff in Inter at 12.8px weight 400. The radius is 6px and padding is 8px 10px. Placement inside a #ffffff0f container supplies the edge. Inputs inherit the frosted language instead of drawing their own outline, so forms read as part of the glass rather than bolted on.

### Gradient Showcase Panel

**Role:** Section backdrop and illustration frame

The system outlier. A violet field runs from #8e64ff into #010314 inside a 24px-radius frame and bleeds behind headlines and the encrypted card illustration. A ciphertext character field is layered at low opacity behind it. It breaks the system's own hue ration on purpose: violet appears at full saturation across hundreds of pixels exactly once per section, as a light source rather than a UI fill.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Roobert at weight 500, 56px for display and 40px for section heads — volume comes from size and -0.02em tracking, not from boldness.
- Keep the canvas at #010314 and lift surfaces with #ffffff0f alpha veils — tonal translucency preserves the indigo undertone that an opaque gray would flatten.
- Make the primary action a #ffffff pill at a 100px radius with #010314 text — the brightest object on a dark page outranks any colored button.
- Ration violet: #8e64ff for toggles, links, glow and one gradient panel, and #6633ee only for 10px badges — a single hue keeps its meaning as "Evervault" because it is scarce.
- Draw structure with 1px #1d1f2e hairlines and "+" crosshair terminals — the engineering-drawing frame does the work that drop shadows do elsewhere.
- Render every encrypted value in ui-monospace at 12px in #ffffff99 — ciphertext is the brand's proof, so it must look like real data.
- Run interior spacing on 10px and 12px and section spacing on 80px — the 2px half-step keeps dense ledgers tight while the page breathes.

### Don't

- Don't set headlines at Roobert 600 or Inter 700 at 56px — the restraint of weight 500 at display sizes is the thesis, and bold headlines turn the vault into a sales banner.
- Don't fill the primary button with #8e64ff — violet is light in this system, and making it the CTA paint spends the entire chromatic budget on one control.
- Don't introduce a second brand hue such as cyan or orange for feature highlights — the budget of one violet plus status-only #3ddc97 is non-negotiable.
- Don't use pure #ffffff for paragraph text — body copy sits at #ffffff99 and headlines at #ffffffe6, and full white flattens a hierarchy that depends on alpha.
- Don't round product tiles to 16px or 24px — 4px corners are what separate the parts catalogue from the 16px showcase cards.
- Don't add soft gray drop shadows to cards on #010314 — they vanish on near-black and muddy the 1px #1d1f2e hairline system.
- Don't decorate with stock illustration or 3D blobs — ornament here is never anything but ciphertext, line-art isometric icons and the single violet gradient.

The rule: cards and tiles carry no shadow. Elevation is a 1px #1d1f2e hairline or an inset light ring, and true drop shadows are reserved for objects that float, such as the primary pill, the knob and the popover.

## Imagery

Evervault uses no photography. Imagery is product mockup and diagrammatic illustration. The hero is a live-styled transaction ledger and configuration panel built from real UI tokens (#0b0d1c fill, 1px #1d1f2e border, 16px radius). The flagship illustration is a violet payment card bearing a mono ciphertext number and a floating "Decryption key" popover with the lg shadow. Processor chips inside mockups use #635bff26, Stripe's purple at 15% alpha; this is mockup-internal and not a system token. Icons are single-weight line-art isometrics drawn in #ffffff99 inside 4px-radius #ffffff0f frames. The violet gradient from #8e64ff to #010314 and the drifting ciphertext character fields are decorative backdrops, not system tokens. Logo rows render partner marks in monochrome #ffffff99. The narrative is that the data is already encrypted and you are only ever looking at ciphertext.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1200px max-width column, and narrower 800px and 647px measures are used for hero copy. Sections are separated by 80px, with up to 120px between major movements. The hero is centered: a 56px two-line Roobert headline, a three-line #ffffff99 subhead and two pills at a 10px gap. Below that run a monochrome logo marquee and a two-column product composition, with the config panel on the left and the ledger on the right. Sections alternate between centered statements and left-aligned headline-plus-paragraph blocks framed by vertical hairlines with rotated "CARD DATA" margin captions. Features run in three columns (Encryption, Payments, Compliance), and developer benefits also use three columns. The nav is a transparent bar holding the wordmark on the left, a floating #0b0d1c capsule in the center and the login and Chalk pill on the right. The footer continues the hairline frame in multi-column link groups. At 375px, use 40px for display and 48px section gaps. Density: comfortable.

## Ciphertext Ornament

The discipline is that every piece of decoration on the page is data. Mono token strings like EV:PA8N:WKD8YHG4, drifting fields of encrypted characters between sections and the card number on the hero illustration all occupy the slots where competitors place abstract shapes or photography. Encryption is shown rather than claimed. The system breaks the moment decorative mono text becomes legible English, switches to a code-editor syntax theme, or rises above 12px and #ffffff99 into headline territory. To extend it, render new illustrations from real product states (a vault entry, a relay log line, a key-rotation event) in ui-monospace at 12px. Keep background character fields at Ash Label alpha or lower, and let Roobert remain the only voice that speaks in sentences at scale.

## Violet Rationing

The page holds exactly one saturated hue, and it behaves as light. #8e64ff glows behind the primary pill at 20% alpha, fills toggles a user has switched on and floods a single gradient panel per section, while #6633ee survives only as 10px badges. Everything else is alpha white on #010314. This is anti-convention for payments brands, which typically paint the primary CTA in brand color. The system breaks when violet becomes a button fill, a card border, a heading color or a second gradient on the same screen. To extend it, ask whether the element is a light source, a user decision or a launch flag. If it is none of those, it takes #ffffff0f, #1d1f2e or #ffffff99 instead.

## Hairline Drafting

Structure is drawn, not cast. Sections are bounded by 1px #1d1f2e verticals running the page height, crossed by horizontals that end in small "+" registration marks, and labeled by rotated uppercase captions in #ffffff80, the vocabulary of a technical drawing. Cards on canvas carry the same 1px line instead of shadow. The system breaks with 2px borders, colored dividers, or soft drop shadows replacing lines on dark surfaces where they cannot be seen. To extend it, add new sections inside the existing vertical frame, use a crosshair wherever two hairlines meet, and reserve real shadows for floating objects only.

## Similar Brands

- **Linear** — Shares the near-black indigo canvas, alpha-white text tiers and a single violet glow used as light. Linear keeps its headlines in Inter, while Evervault switches to Roobert at weight 500.
- **Stripe** — The same category of payments infrastructure, with product UI rendered as the hero proof. Stripe runs on a light canvas with multi-hue gradients, where Evervault rations one violet on #010314.
- **Vercel** — Shares the 1px hairline grid with crosshair registration marks and inverted white primary pills on black. Vercel is achromatic, while Evervault adds violet.
- **Basis Theory** — A direct competitor in card tokenization and vaulting with a developer-first dark presentation. Evervault leans harder on ciphertext as visual ornament.
- **Resend** — Shares the developer-dark composition of centered display headlines, monochrome logo marquees and frosted glass tiles at single-digit alpha.
